title: POC scoping: Acme Health - Security pilot
customer_attendees: Dr. Sarah Johnson (Head of Data Platform)
summary: POC scoping focused on security and compliance requirements for a pilot with Acme Health. Discussed SOC 2/ISO attestation, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logging, workload sizing for benchmarks, success criteria, and timelines. Agreed next steps: share security docs, schedule benchmark, and kickoff pilot week of 2025-09-22.
topics: SSO / SAML integration and IdP requirements
action_items: Evan: Share SOC 2 and ISO27001 attestation PDFs and security questionnaire by 2025-09-14
Priya: Schedule 48-hour dedicated benchmark (500 concurrent sessions target) and send invite by 2025-09-16
Emily: Provide sample workload traces and expected 95th perc latency targets by 2025-09-15
Rohit: Send list of required audit log fields and retention policy constraints by 2025-09-14
next_steps: Redwood to provide SOC2/ISO docs + security questionnaire
Kickoff benchmark on Redwood Dedicated with Acme's sample traces
SSO/SAML integration dry-run in staging environment
Confirm pilot success criteria and SLAs, then sign POC engagement
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~58m | Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SE), Dr. Sarah Johnson, Rohit Mehra, Emily Park, Marcus Lee

00:00 Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Evan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. we've got Priya and Liam from the solutions team. how's everyone doing?
00:06 Sarah: doing well, thanks. excited to get into the security details. we run in healthcare so compliance is, uh, obviously a big deal.
00:12 Evan: absolutely. the goal for today is to scope the POC — specifically the security and compliance requirements for the pilot, and then nail down workload sizing and benchmarks, and agree on timelines and success criteria. sound right?
00:22 Sarah: yes. Rohit is our security lead, he'll take point on requirements. Rohit, do you want to intro your constraints?
00:27 Rohit: sure. so primary items: SOC 2 type II is mandatory, we also want ISO 27001 if you have it. SSO via SAML is required, we need RBAC with audit logs exported to our SIEM (Splunk), and encryption KMS integration, ideally customer-managed keys. retention for logs is 7 years for some records per our policy.
00:45 Priya: okay good. we support SOC 2 attestation and ISO 27001; we can share the reports and our security questionnaire. for SSO we have a SAML integration guide and support both IdP initiated and SP initiated flows. for RBAC we have role templates and can map to your corporate roles, and audit logs can be streamed to your endpoint.
01:03 Marcus: quick question on audit logs — do you capture token-level request details, and can we filter by user-id and model route?
01:09 Liam: yes we capture per-request metadata, token counts, timing, route, model version. sometimes the names in the transcription show up weird, but in the logs it's structured: user_id, session_id, request_id, model, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, status. we can export JSON to your SIEM via HTTPS forwarder or S3.
01:27 Rohit: what's your retention on the vendor side? can we set a TTL so data doesn't persist beyond our retention window?
01:33 Priya: we have configurable retention per customer; for Private/VPC customers you can choose our rolling TTL or we can set up a lifecycle policy on exported logs. default hosted retention is 90 days but we can extend or provide export for compliance.
01:45 Emily: from an engineering side, the pilot's success criteria include: parity in latency compared to our internal baseline (95th perc under 250ms for short prompts), throughput of X requests per second — roughly 500 concurrent user sessions, and model output quality matching our current model. we also need zero data leakage during the pilot.
02:04 Evan: good specifics. can you share your baseline traces and 95th perc numbers? that will help us size the Dedicated pool for the benchmark.
02:13 Emily: yes we'll send traces — they are about 10k requests over 24h, with spikes during business hours to 600 rps. average payload is ~450 tokens per session.
02:23 Priya: for the benchmark we'll replicate that distribution. suggested initial POC: 48 hour dedicated run with 500-600 concurrent sessions, run both quantized and non-quantized model variants to measure latency and token cost.
02:37 Sarah: timeline question — we need the POC live before the end of September or it's hard to hit our internal approval schedule. is that feasible?
02:44 Evan: yes we think so. plan: share security docs by Mon (2025-09-14), get SAML test accounts and network whitelists from your side, schedule benchmark to start 2025-09-22, run for 48 hours, then a results review 2025-09-25.
02:58 Rohit: about SAML — we need assertion mapping for groups to RBAC roles. do you support SCIM for automated provisioning?
03:05 Priya: SCIM is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted we can do SAML group mapping and manual mapping. for the POC we can do group-to-role mapping and if you want we can enable SCIM in the pilot staging if your IdP supports it.
03:22 Marcus: KMS integration — can we use our own KMS?
03:25 Liam: yes, for Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). for Dedicated we have options to integrate with your cloud KMS or use a bring-your-own key approach. we can document the steps in the security playbook.
03:39 Rohit: perfect. one more: do you have SOC 2 audit logs that show access to logs and admin actions? our auditors will want proof of admin activity and RBAC changes.
03:47 Priya: yes, audit logs include admin actions, role changes, policy updates. we also can produce exportable reports for audit purposes.
03:56 Emily: back to workload sizing — are there recommended batch sizes or KV cache configurations to hit the latency numbers?
04:01 Liam: yes, recommended continuous batching parameters depend on your latency SLO. for 95th < 250ms we recommend smaller batch sizes and aggressive KV caching for repeated prefixes. in the benchmark we will test batching profiles and quantization options and report the cost/latency tradeoffs.
04:18 Sarah: how do you handle fallbacks? e.g., if Dedicated pool is saturated can requests failover to hosted? we need predictable behavior.
04:25 Evan: you can configure routing policies — canary to lower cost models or fallback to hosted with cryptographic isolation disabled based on contract. for the POC we recommend pinning the model to avoid variability, and enabling a hard cap to prevent spillover unless you want failover.
04:40 Rohit: on data residency — all inference in the pilot needs to run in our region (us-east-1). can you guarantee region pinning?
04:47 Priya: yes, Dedicated pools can be provisioned in a chosen region. for Hosted we can route to specific regions but it's less strict. for the pilot we'll use a Dedicated pool in us-east-1.
04:57 Emily: what's the expected token cost so we can estimate spend during the benchmark?
05:01 Evan: depends on model and quantization. we'll produce a projected cost spreadsheet. rough back-of-envelope: with your avg payload 450 tokens and 10k requests over 24h, during 48h pilot it's about 20k requests -> ~9M tokens in/out; we'll model cost across quantized vs fp16 and share numbers.
05:20 Sarah: ok. please include per-token and per-request estimates and an estimate for dedicated capacity monthly commit so we can budget.
05:28 Evan: will do.
05:30 Rohit: about the security docs, for auditors we need: SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001 cert, penetration testing summary, encryption at rest details, key management doc, and the security questionnaire filled out.
05:41 Priya: we'll attach the SOC2 and ISO certs, a redacted pentest summary, and a completed security questionnaire. we'll also include the SAML guide and RBAC mapping examples.
05:52 Marcus: if we need log forwarding to Splunk, what's the format?
05:55 Liam: JSON lines, with documented schema. we'll send the schema and an example bundle.
06:02 Emily: can we get a staging SAML SP entity to test without impacting prod?
06:06 Evan: yes we'll provision a staging environment for the POC. share the IdP metadata and SAML test accounts and we'll configure.
06:12 Rohit: any SLA during pilot? we want at least 99.5% env availability and timely support.
06:18 Evan: for POC we'll provide priority support; Dedicated comes with SLA options. we'll propose a temporary SLA for the pilot and include on-call contacts.
06:25 Sarah: great. next up, who owns what — recap.
06:29 Evan: recap: Redwood will share SOC2/ISO/pen test + security questionnaire by 2025-09-14; Redwood to schedule benchmark (Priya) by 2025-09-16 and kickoff 2025-09-22; Acme to share traces, IdP metadata, and audit log field requirements by 2025-09-15. after benchmark, review results and decide on expansion.
06:47 Rohit: sounds good, i'll review the docs when you send. any gotchas we should be aware of?
06:51 Priya: sometimes token accounting differs slightly across quantization; we'll call out any measurement diffs. also transcriptions may have some mislabeling but logs are authoritative.
06:59 Emily: ok thanks.
07:01 Evan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links: SOC2 PDF, ISO27001 cert, security questionnaire (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/sq-acme), SAML guide (link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/saml), and benchmark plan spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/acme-draft).
07:18 Sarah: thanks all.
07:20 [meeting ended]

Notes: transcript contains some ASR errors and occasional speaker mislabels; action items captured above. Attachments referenced: https://redwood.example.com/security/sq-acme (security questionnaire), https://redwood.example.com/docs/saml (SAML integration guide), and benchmark spreadsheet link.
